title: Break-glass grant operation, central ledger fault point and SIT evidence are not named for the 19-service target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 039 Access log into the decision log and break glass admin v1.md (sections 3, 7, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 20 and 28; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story activates break-glass with POST /admin/break-glass, reads the access log with GET /admin/access-log and writes one decision log entry in the caller transaction, and AC7 fails the read when the decision log store is unavailable. In the target the grant and the access log belong to P4 rwb-access (Ownership Map rows POST /admin/break-glass-grants and GET /admin/access-log), every service writes its own local decision record in its own schema and publishes DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1, and the central ledger in P7 rwb-decision is complete within five minutes (DP-03; Arch v5 slide 28). The target therefore needs three things the sources do not name: the grant operation to call in the pack, the point at which the local record write is forced to fail, and the SIT evidence location.
evidence: RWB-E1-039 section 12 (POST /admin/break-glass, GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/access-log, GET /api/recovery/v1/decision-log, published interface AccessEventPublisher) and section 7 AC7; Arch v5 slide 28 (local record then central ledger, five-minute completeness) and slide 14 (rwb-access owns the access log, rwb-decision owns the central ledger); Ownership Map api rows POST /admin/break-glass-grants, GET /admin/access-log and GET /decision-log.
proposed: Name the grant operation, the local-record fault point and the evidence location at the integration pack review before the SIT run; keep the window, the incident pattern and the reason length as parameter values.

title: Reference-load owner, field-ID check and template body storage move in the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 046 Template and merge field catalog as data v1.md (sections 3, 11, 12 and 13); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
description: The legacy story says P4 owns POST /admin/reference-loads, reads sys_fields through the P4 reference data interface and keeps the template body reference with the template. In the target the Ownership Map puts the reference-load operations on P3 rwb-case (POST /admin/reference-loads, POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify, POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback), the entity and field registry on P1 rwb-source-data (GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields), template and merge_field with P6 rwb-comms and the document body with P5 rwb-document. The sources name neither the service that performs the field-ID check, nor where the body file is held, nor how the approval of a version is written to the decision log.
evidence: RWB-E1-046 sections 3, 11, 12 and 13 (POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads, P4 owns the endpoint, sys_fields check, template.body_ref); Ownership Map api rows POST /admin/reference-loads owner P3, GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields owner P1, GET /admin/templates owner P6, POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents owner P5, and tables sys_fields owner P1, template and merge_field owner P6, document owner P5; Arch v5 slide 17 (P6 and P5 contracts) and slide 41.
area: Reference data and template catalog integration
proposed: Keep a load with any refused row refused in full, put the field-ID check behind the P1 data dictionary contract and the body behind P5, and record one decision record per version approval.

title: Feature-flag owner, flag operations and the weekly report trigger move in the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 047 Feature flags for module release with a removal date v1.md (sections 3, 4, 12 and 13); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44
description: The legacy story puts the two flag tables and the four flag endpoints in module P2 Integration and runs the weekly removal report as a Quartz job on Monday 08:00. In the target the Ownership Map puts feature_flag and feature_flag_change with the platform library (PLT) and names the four flag operations as PLT operations (GET /feature-flags, GET /admin/feature-flags, POST /admin/feature-flags, PATCH /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}), DP-10 replaces Quartz with a Temporal Schedule and DP-14 replaces the legacy rwb.p n dot and rwb.casewf dot names with the per-service names. The sources name neither the base that serves the platform flag operations, nor the Schedule identifier of the weekly report, nor whether the four legacy flag keys are renamed in the data.
evidence: RWB-E1-047 sections 3, 4, 12 and 13 (two tables, four endpoints, Quartz Monday 08:00 report); Ownership Map tables feature_flag and feature_flag_change owner PLT and api rows for the four flag operations owner PLT; Template and Rules v1 section R3 default ruling (feature flags to the platform library); Arch v5 slide 44 (no shared Quartz tables, Schedules in the owning service); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-10 and DP-14.
proposed: Serve the flag operations from the platform library through gateway-bff, keep every value as a data row, and run the weekly report as a Temporal Schedule in the same service with every message and status unchanged.

title: OCR trigger, worker count and parameter home change in the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 049 OCR pipeline on the Workbench document hub v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 42 and 44; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
description: The legacy story runs the OCR step as a Quartz job every 15 minutes with OCR_WORKERS equal to four and holds its four parameters in document_hub_parameter inside the document module. In the target JOB-12 is owned by P5 rwb-document with the mechanism event plus KEDA workers (Arch v5 slide 44) inside DocumentIntakeWorkflow, the intake item is created from the DocumentStored event (EV-16) and deduped through the inbox, and DP-06 sends parameters to the P3 rwb-case contract. document_hub_parameter is still owned by P5 under the Ownership Map, so the four OCR parameters have two possible homes and the sources do not say which the target uses, nor what OCR_WORKERS means once the worker count scales on queue depth.
evidence: RWB-E1-049 sections 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13 (OCR_MIN_QUALITY, OCR_WORKERS, OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS, JOB-12 every 15 minutes, document_hub_parameter); Arch v5 slide 16 (DocumentIntakeWorkflow: OCR, classify, extract), slide 42 row 16 (DocumentStored), slide 44 (JOB-12 event plus KEDA workers); Ownership Map table document_hub_parameter owner P5; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-06, DP-09 and DP-10.
proposed: Keep the four OCR parameters in the document hub parameter table that the map names, read them as data, treat OCR_WORKERS as the worker concurrency cap while the platform scales workers on queue depth, and keep the 60-minute target.

title: Classifier route, parameter home and agent run evidence are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 050 Document classification v1.md (sections 3, 4, 6, 11 and 12); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 12 Contract; 12.5 Workflows and activities
description: The legacy story reaches the classifier through the P10 model gateway from inside the document intake job and holds CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD, CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES and CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS in document_hub_parameter. In the target P5 rwb-document runs the classify step and P10 rwb-agent serves the model call through AgentRunWorkflow (60 seconds then rule result, Arch v5 slide 16), so the classify step is a child run on the rwb-agent task queue; document_hub_parameter is still owned by P5 under the Ownership Map while DP-06 sends parameters to the P3 rwb-case contract. The sources name neither the route that serves the model call, nor where the three parameters live in the target, nor which evidence of the agent run the pack may read.
evidence: RWB-E1-050 sections 3, 4, 6, 11 and 12 (classifier through the P10 model gateway, CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD, CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES, CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, ClassifierClient, ClassificationReader); Arch v5 slide 16 (P10 IN AgentRunWorkflow 60 s then rule result; P5 IN AgentRunCompleted for classification) and slide 41; Ownership Map table document_hub_parameter owner P5, api rows GET /admin/agent-runs owner P10 and GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields owner P1; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-06, DP-10 and DP-11.
proposed: Run the classify step as a child run of rwb-agent, keep the three parameters as data rows in the table the map names, and keep the 0.80 threshold, the 90 percent accuracy target and the type labels unchanged.
